transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morris (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Priya Singh (Halcyon Head of Security), Markus Vela (Platform), Sofia Ruiz (DevOps), Ben Carter (PM)

Summary (auto):
Initial security posture discovery focused on encryption and key management, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable throughput but has regulatory constraints that may push Private/VPC for certain workloads. Action items captured: share SOC 2 and ISO docs, KMS/BYOK integration walkthrough, schedule technical deep dive.

Topics: SOC2/ISO scope, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC model, audit log retention and forwarding, encryption (at-rest/in-transit/CMK), hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), data residency and retention windows, SIEM integration, onboarding pilot scope.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena Morris: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — this is Lena from Redwood, with Devon our SE and Maya who helps with onboarding.
[00:09] Priya Singh: Hi, Priya here. I'll be leading the security review from Halcyon.
[00:12] Markus Vela: Markus — platform eng.
[00:14] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, DevOps.
[00:16] Ben Carter: Ben, product.
[00:18] Lena: Awesome. High level — would love to understand your constraints and what would make you comfortable running inference with Redwood. Priya, do you want to kick off with the security checklist?
[00:29] Priya: Sure. Topline: we need SOC 2 type II, ISO27001 evidence, SSO with SAML + SCIM provisioning, strict RBAC, encrypted keys with customer-managed option ideally, and the ability to forward audit logs to our Sumo/Elastic stack. Also retention windows — we have 7 year retention on some PII audit trails but for ML telemetry we usually do 90 to 365 days depending on classification.
[00:52] Lena: Great, thanks. We have SOC 2 and ISO material, and BYOK via KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated depending on config. Devon, want to add details on KMS?
[01:03] Devon Park: Yeah. So we support both Redwood-hosted keys and customer-managed keys. For Hosted API customers typically use our managed encryption unless they need BYOK — for Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) or an HSM in VPC. There's a couple of modes: envelope encryption with CMKs for model artifacts and KV cache, and TLS in transit. Webhook/forwarding of audit logs can be done over syslog or S3 bucket delivery.
[01:34] Priya: When you say KV cache, is that persisted unencrypted or in memory only? We cannot have sensitive context persisted unencrypted.
[01:42] Devon: KV cache is persisted to disk for warm restarts but encrypted using the CMK. For Hosted, it's in our storage layer encrypted with our key; for BYOK we wrap with your CMK. There's a small caveat around swap files and OS-level caches — for Private we can ensure no host-level persistence outside encrypted volumes.
[02:02] Sofia: Are there options to keep logs within our VPC? We want log ingestion to remain in our account.
[02:07] Devon: For Private (VPC/air-gapped) yes. For Dedicated we offer a cross-account log sink to your S3 or push to your SIEM via secure forwarder. Hosted has streaming options but typically goes to Redwood-managed storage unless you opt-in for log exports.
[02:22] Markus: Latency is sensitive for a subset of our calls — 40ms p99 target — does Dedicated help here?
[02:29] Lena: Dedicated gets you pinned GPU pools and lower jitter. Devon: Also model routing and local regional placement helps. There is a cost tradeoff vs Hosted.
[02:39] Ben: If we do Dedicated with BYOK, can we still do periodic model rollouts and verifications through Redwood console?
[02:45] Devon: Yes, the deployment abstraction is the same. You get the same console features — rollouts, canary, A/B. The only difference is where the nodes live and who controls the key.
[02:55] Priya: SSO — SAML and SCIM for provisioning. We need SCIM to auto-provision service accounts and RBAC groups. What role granularity do you support?
[03:05] Maya Chen: We map to role groups: account-admin, security-auditor, infra-operator, app-engineer, read-only. SCIM integrates to maintain group membership. Devon, the fine-grain?
[03:15] Devon: Roles can be scoped by project/route/model. We also support custom roles for Enterprise—you can define a set of permissions and map to SCIM groups. Audit trails capture role changes.
[03:24] Priya: How immutable are audit logs? We need tamper-evidence for compliance.
[03:29] Devon: Logs are write-once in our storage and can be exported to your immutable S3 with object lock or forwarded to your SIEM. For Private you can ingest directly into your storage. We also publish daily cryptographic digests for integrity checks if you want a signed attest.
[03:45] Priya: Okay that helps. Any certifications around physical security for private/on-prem package?
[03:51] Lena: Our private deploy supports being installed behind your firewall on hardware you control; Redwood assists with support but physical security in that scenario is your responsibility. For our Redwood-managed regions we inherit cloud provider compliance; we can share our env details in the SOC packet.
[04:06] Sofia: What about data retention defaults? We can't keep user prompts for longer than 30 days for certain classes. Can we set per-project retention?
[04:14] Devon: Yes, retention is per-route or per-project. Hosted has default 30 days for telemetry with options to extend. You can also disable retention for certain routes to avoid storing prompts at all — in that case we use ephemeral mode where we don't persist bodies beyond what the model runtime needs.
[04:30] Ben: If we disable retention, how does that impact caching and cost?
[04:34] Devon: Disabling retention disables prefix/KV caching which can increase per-token compute cost and latency for repeated context. For many production workloads, selective caching gives best economics.
[04:44] Markus: Regarding keys — does Redwood require access to our plaintext keys during onboarding?
[04:48] Devon: No. For BYOK integration we use key wrapping — Redwood never has plaintext CMKs. The service uses KMS APIs to perform encryption operations; only ciphertext and encrypted envelopes are stored.
[04:58] Priya: Is HSM BYOK supported for on-prem HSMs too?
[05:02] Devon: We can integrate with customer HSMs for Private deployments. For Dedicated there's support for cloud HSMs (CloudHSM, CloudKMS with HSM-backed keys). We'll need a technical deep dive to validate network and PKCS11 bindings.
[05:18] Lena: Switching to audit: What volume are you expecting? Number of calls, tokens, concurrency?
[05:25] Ben: Initially 5k calls/day, peak to 20k during launches. Token size varies but average short prompts — maybe 150 tokens.
[05:34] Devon: That's modest. Logs volume will be mostly request/response metadata and model traces if you opt-in. We can stream per-request logs or aggregated metrics.
[05:44] Priya: We require per-request full metadata for forensics. Can you provide full request ID, route, calling user, model, and token counts in logs?
[05:53] Devon: Yes, we can surface request-id, user-id (or obfuscated service account), route, model-version, latency, token counts, and if enabled, reason codes for fallback.
[06:03] Sofia: How do you handle PII detection and scrub before logs?
[06:06] Devon: We have optional PII scrubbing pipelines that can redact sensitive fields using regex and ML detectors — you can configure rules. For high-sensitivity you can route raw logs into your own bucket and run scrubbing on your side.
[06:19] Priya: Are there any multi-tenant isolation guarantees for Hosted?
[06:23] Devon: Hosted is multi-tenant logically isolated; we provide strong tenant boundaries at the routing and storage layer but for the highest isolation Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[06:33] Priya: For compliance we need a runbook for breach notification and incident handling. Do you have an incident response SLA?
[06:41] Lena: We have documented incident response, can share the runbook. For Enterprise customers on contract we can agree on notification timelines.
[06:49] Priya: Please send that.
[06:52] Lena: Will do.
[06:54] Ben: A few product questions: model rollback — if a model update causes regression we need quick rollback. Can Redwood automate fallback to an earlier model?
[07:03] Devon: Yes, we support automatic fallback policies and instant rollbacks via the console or API. You can pin a route to a model version.
[07:10] Ben: Awesome.
[07:12] Priya: Any third party pen test results you can share?
[07:15] Lena: We have a summary and remediation distro from our recent pentest, we'll include the redacted report in the packet.
[07:22] Markus: Network-wise, for Dedicated what are the egress/ingress expectations and do we need to open specific ports?
[07:30] Devon: For Dedicated we typically establish secure peering and TLS over standard ports. For Private you may require additional config for control-plane connectivity if you choose Redwood-managed control plane — otherwise fully air-gapped deploy removes outbound. We'll include a network diagram in the follow-up.
[07:45] Sofia: Can you integrate with our IAM for short-lived certs or do you rely on long-lived API keys?
[07:51] Devon: We support short-lived tokens via OIDC exchange and service accounts using rotating keys. Long-lived API keys are also supported but we recommend short-lived for production.
[07:59] Priya: Any limitations on encryption libraries or FIPS requirements?
[08:02] Devon: For FIPS workloads we recommend Private deployments where your stack can enforce FIPS-validated crypto. Our cloud offering uses industry-standard TLS and FIPS-compliant ciphers where the underlying cloud supports them. We'll flag any gaps in the follow-up.
[08:18] Lena: Quick note on retention again — you said some domains need seven years. We can set archival export to your storage for long-term retention while keeping hot telemetry short-lived.
[08:28] Priya: That pattern would work.
[08:30] Ben: Pricing — if we run a pilot for 3 months at moderate volume what does that look like?
[08:35] Lena: We typically propose a small Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity and a discount off committed spend. I'll follow up with a tailored estimate.
[08:42] Markus: One more on auditability: do you provide user-level action logs for console/API (e.g., model deploys, role changes)?
[08:49] Devon: Yes, console and API actions are logged with actor, timestamp, IP, and diff. Those are part of the audit export.
[08:57] Priya: On SCIM mapping — can we map AD groups to project scopes?
[09:02] Devon: Yes, SCIM group attributes can map to project scopes; we'll show example mappings in the docs.
[09:09] Sofia: Is there a test harness or sandbox for us to run sample traffic and verify end-to-end before signing?
[09:15] Maya: We provide sandbox tokens and a shared test environment for pilots; SE will help set up a telemetry dashboard.
[09:21] Priya: Ok, I'd like to request: 1) SOC2 + ISO docs, 2) incident response runbook, 3) KMS BYOK integration guide and sample terraform, 4) network diagram and ports list, 5) pricing for a 3-month dedicated pilot.
[09:41] Lena: We'll get those over. Devon, anything you want to add before we wrap?
[09:46] Devon: I'll add that for Private deployments we'll need to schedule a session with your infra team to validate HSM bindings and network. Also I'll prepare a short matrix showing tradeoffs: Hosted=fastest time-to-value, Dedicated=predictable latency and cost, Private=maximum control/compliance.
[10:05] Priya: One small nit — logs immutability and object lock is key for us. We'll need instructions for enabling object lock on S3 exports.
[10:13] Devon: Noted, we'll include S3 object-lock config examples.
[10:17] Ben: Sounds good.
[10:19] Lena: Great. We'll follow up with the packet and set up the technical deep dive. Appreciate the time.
[10:24] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[10:26] Markus: Thanks.
[10:27] Sofia: Bye.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
